name: DOE Science Undergraduate Laboratory Internships (SULI)
description: 10-week research internships at DOE national laboratories. Students work with lab staff on projects in energy, physics, materials, computing, and more.
deadline_notes: Applications open in fall and spring
eligibility: U.S. citizens/permanent residents enrolled in undergraduate programs

name: NSF Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU)
description: Summer research programs at universities across the U.S. covering virtually every STEM field. Students conduct independent research with faculty mentors.
eligibility: U.S. citizens/permanent residents, undergraduate students

name: NASA Internships
description: Internships at NASA centers across the country in aerospace, robotics, software, data science, mechanical, electrical, and more. Fall, spring, and summer sessions.
eligibility: U.S. citizens currently enrolled in accredited programs

name: ORISE Research Fellowships
org: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education
description: Broad catalog of fellowship and internship programs at federal agencies including DOE, CDC, FDA, EPA, and more. Covers nearly every STEM discipline.
deadline_notes: Varies by position, listings on Zintellect
eligibility: Varies by position; most require U.S. citizenship

name: National Defense Science and Engineering Graduate Fellowship (NDSEG)
description: Highly competitive 3-year graduate fellowship covering full tuition, fees, and a stipend. For students pursuing doctoral degrees in STEM fields relevant to national defense.
eligibility: U.S. citizens applying to or enrolled in a doctoral program

name: Hertz Fellowship
description: One of the most prestigious graduate fellowships in STEM — provides up to 5 years of funding for PhD students who show exceptional potential in the applied physical and engineering sciences.
eligibility: U.S. citizens or permanent residents, graduate school applicants

name: NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program (GRFP)
description: NSF's flagship graduate fellowship — 3 years of funding for graduate students in any STEM field. One of the most widely recognized fellowships in academia.
eligibility: U.S. citizens/permanent residents, early-career graduate students or seniors

name: SMART Scholarship-for-Service Program
description: Full scholarship plus stipend for STEM students in exchange for post-graduation service as a civilian employee at a DoD facility. Covers undergrad and graduate students.
deadline_notes: Applications open December, close in late winter
eligibility: U.S. citizens, pursuing STEM degrees

name: AIAA Student Design Competitions
org: American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics (AIAA)
description: Multiple annual design competitions including aircraft design, spacecraft design, and engine design. Teams submit technical reports and present at AIAA forums.
deadline_notes: Varies by competition; typically fall submissions
eligibility: Undergraduate and graduate student teams

name: SAE Collegiate Design Series
description: Hands-on engineering design competitions including Formula SAE, Baja SAE, Aero Design, and Clean Snowmobile Challenge. Teams design, build, and race/demonstrate vehicles.
deadline_notes: Registration typically opens in fall for spring events
eligibility: Undergraduate student teams

name: NASA Lunabotics Competition
description: Annual robotics competition where teams design and build robots to mine simulated lunar regolith. Strong emphasis on systems engineering, autonomy, and space applications.
deadline_notes: Registration typically opens in fall, event held in spring
eligibility: Undergraduate and graduate teams at accredited U.S. institutions

name: RoboNation Competitions (RoboSub, RoboBoat, etc.)
description: Autonomous systems competitions including RoboSub (underwater), RoboBoat (surface), and others. Strong focus on autonomy, computer vision, and systems integration.
eligibility: University student teams worldwide

name: ASCE/AISC Student Steel Bridge Competition
description: Teams design, fabricate, and construct a scaled steel bridge that is judged on structural performance, construction speed, stiffness, deflection, weight, and economy.
deadline_notes: Regional events in spring, national event follows
eligibility: Undergraduate student teams

name: AGU Osher Lifelong Learning Hydropower Competition
description: Student competitions in earth and space sciences covering hydrology, geophysics, atmospheric science, ocean science, and related fields.
eligibility: Graduate and undergraduate students

name: MathWorks Mini Drone Competition
description: Teams use MATLAB and Simulink to program autonomous control algorithms for a mini drone. Tests skills in control systems, simulation, and embedded code generation.
eligibility: Undergraduate and graduate teams

name: EcoCAR EV Challenge
org: U.S. Department of Energy / GM / MathWorks
description: Multi-year student competition to design and build next-generation electric vehicles. Covers battery systems, controls, software, and vehicle integration.
deadline_notes: Teams apply to join the 4-year program
eligibility: Selected university teams across North America

name: IEEEXtreme Programming Competition
description: Annual 24-hour online programming competition for IEEE student members. Teams solve algorithm and data structures problems in any language.
eligibility: IEEE student members, teams of up to 3

name: ICPC — International Collegiate Programming Contest
description: The world's largest and most prestigious collegiate programming competition. Teams of three solve complex algorithmic problems under time pressure.
deadline_notes: Regional contests in fall, World Finals in spring
eligibility: Undergraduate students, teams of 3

name: Google Summer of Code (GSoC)
description: Paid summer program where students contribute to open source organizations under the mentorship of experienced developers. One of the most respected open-source programs in the world.
eligibility: Students 18+ worldwide

name: Major League Hacking (MLH) Fellowship
description: Remote 12-week fellowship where participants contribute to open source projects or build software with a startup. Paid stipend included.
eligibility: Students and recent graduates worldwide

name: Outreachy
description: Paid remote internships contributing to open source and open science projects. Specifically supports underrepresented groups in tech.
deadline_notes: Two cohorts per year, applications in February and September
eligibility: Underrepresented groups in tech; open internationally

name: DARPA Riser Program
description: Identifies and engages rising stars in science and engineering who are doing innovative early-stage research with potential defense applications.
eligibility: PhD students and early postdocs nominated by advisors

name: DOE Computational Science Graduate Fellowship (CSGF)
description: 4-year fellowship for PhD students using high-performance computing to solve complex science and engineering problems. Includes a practicum at a DOE national lab.
eligibility: U.S. citizens/permanent residents applying to or in a PhD program

name: SEA Semester
description: Academic semester programs combining shore-based study with 30+ days at sea conducting oceanographic research aboard tall ships.
eligibility: Undergraduate students at accredited institutions

name: ACS Scholars Program
description: Renewable scholarships for underrepresented minority undergraduate students studying chemistry or chemistry-related fields.
eligibility: Underrepresented minority undergraduates in chemistry-related majors, U.S. citizens

name: AIAA Foundation Graduate Awards
org: American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics
description: Graduate scholarships and awards for students pursuing aerospace sciences and engineering. Multiple award types covering different specializations.
eligibility: Graduate students in aerospace-related fields, AIAA student members

name: NIST Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship (SURF)
org: National Institute of Standards and Technology
description: Summer research at NIST laboratories in Gaithersburg, MD or Boulder, CO. Projects span measurement science, physics, materials, chemistry, engineering, and more.
eligibility: U.S. citizens/permanent residents, undergraduate students

name: Sandia National Laboratories Internships
description: Research and engineering internships at Sandia's labs in Albuquerque and Livermore. Work spans nuclear security, energy, materials, computing, and systems engineering.
deadline_notes: Rolling applications, apply by November for summer
eligibility: U.S. citizens with ability to obtain a security clearance

name: SpaceX Internship Program
description: Hands-on engineering internships in avionics, structures, propulsion, software, manufacturing, and more. Fast-paced, high-ownership environment.
deadline_notes: Rolling, apply at least 6 months ahead
eligibility: U.S. citizens/permanent residents, undergraduate or graduate

name: Los Alamos National Lab Computational & Data Science Internship
description: Summer internships focused on high-performance computing, data science, machine learning, and scientific simulation at one of the nation's top national labs.
eligibility: U.S. citizens/permanent residents

name: HackMIT / Major League Hacking Events
description: Hundreds of hackathons annually — in-person and virtual. MLH-sanctioned events offer prizes, networking, and recruiting from top tech companies.
deadline_notes: Year-round events, check mlh.io for current listings
eligibility: Students worldwide

name: Devpost Hackathons
description: Platform hosting hundreds of online and in-person hackathons with cash prizes. Sponsored by companies like AWS, Google, Microsoft, and more.
eligibility: Open to students and professionals worldwide

name: ASME Student Design Competition
description: Annual design competition with a new theme each year. Teams design, build, and demonstrate mechanical devices that meet specific performance criteria.
deadline_notes: Registration and qualifier events in fall/spring
eligibility: Undergraduate ASME student member teams

name: Cleantech Open Accelerator
description: Startup accelerator and competition for clean technology ventures. Teams get mentorship, access to investors, and compete for cash prizes.
eligibility: Early-stage startups, student teams welcome

name: Lemelson-MIT Student Prize
description: Awards teams of undergraduate and graduate students who create inventions that improve lives. Strong focus on inventiveness, creativity, and social impact.
eligibility: U.S. college students, team or individual

name: HPE Coding Challenge
description: Software engineering challenges focused on HPC, storage, and cloud computing. Prizes and potential recruiting pathways.
eligibility: Students worldwide

name: Presidential Management Fellows (PMF) Program
description: Highly competitive 2-year fellowship for advanced degree candidates interested in federal government careers across all agencies and disciplines.
eligibility: U.S. citizens who have completed or are completing an advanced degree
